gam-math-uc-001-q1.reason: An independent adjudicator, shown the pack's questions without its source, could settle this question using gam-math-uc-001-q2, gam-math-uc-001-q3. Two independent sibling channels settle it. (1) q2 asks for the uncertainty in the area of a rectangle whose sides are each good to 1 per cent, and its options are 0.5, 1, 2 per cent. Quadrature would give 1.4 per cent, which is absent; 2 per cent is the linear sum of relative uncertainties. So the pack's convention is linear addition, which forces 0.5 here and rules out 0.36 — the source's combination rule is recovered from a sibling's option list. (2) q3's correct answer states that the uncertainty is rounded to one significant figure. Under the pack's own stated formatting rule, '± 0.25' and '± 0.36' are not writable results at all, killing b and c for a reason that has nothing to do with the two rods. Between the survivors a and d, a is the transparent subtract-the-uncertainties trap. Answer forced without reading the source.
